title: Mexico Will Promote Technological Cooperation with China to Generate Energy from Waste
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by[La Jornada Editorial
Staff](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/la%20redacci%C3%B3n) originally
appeared in the [November 15, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/15/politica/semarnat-
mexico-impulsara-cooperacion-tecnologica-con-china-para-generar-energia-con-
desechos), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** Mexico seeks to draw on China’s experience in waste
management, energy generation from waste and wastewater treatment using
artificial intelligence, as part of efforts to promote the circular economy
and recover public spaces for communities in our country, reported Secretary
of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat) Alicia Bárcena.

Ahead of Mexico’s upcoming participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic
Cooperation (APEC) forum summit, to be held in China, the official visited
various facilities specializing in waste utilization and the restoration of
bodies of water over the weekend, to explore their application to ecosystem
restoration and the cleanup of our rivers in the country.

On her social media, Bárcena explained that, on instructions from President
Claudia Sheinbaum, who heads the Mexican delegation at the APEC summit, she
made these visits to promote technological cooperation with the Asian giant
and develop solutions that would also allow organic waste —including
sargassum— to be used to generate energy and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

In Zhuhai, the head of Semarnat visited the SUS Environment company’s plant,
which she said has the capacity to process **3,000 metric tons of waste a day
and generate up to 90 megawatts of electricity**. The official emphasized that
China went from recovering energy from 9.8 percent of its urban waste in 2005
to 84.6 percent in 2024, while disposal in landfills fell from 85 to 5
percent.

In Shenzhen, the host city of the annual summit, she toured the Dasha River,
which went from a polluted waterway to an ecological corridor and a “sponge
city” more than 14 kilometers long, through cleanup, environmental restoration
and the recovery of public spaces, she indicated.

She also visited the **underground Honghu plant** , with the capacity to
process 100,000 metric tons of wastewater a day and artificial intelligence
systems to optimize its operation; above ground, the facility has a public
park, she explained.

“Shenzhen is also an example of how to recover rivers, restore ecosystems and
transform previously polluted spaces into places where communities can meet
and spend time together!” the Mexican official emphasized.

In this city, she also visited the **Nanshan Energy Ecological Park** , where
she learned about a model for using waste to generate energy, recover
materials and create public spaces.

> “China’s experience shows that it is possible to leave landfills behind and
> move toward a circular economy model,” she said.
